Application    Sheet No. 5

Application is hereby made for the disposal of letters and newspapers which were subsequently delivered to P.A. 618 Yu Yuen Road the premises of which the S.M.P. raided on the 7/9/31 and seized a quantity of Communistic papers.

List of mails delivered at No P.A. 618 Yu Yuen Road since Sept. 7th 1931 when the premises were raided by the Municipal Police on the authority of a search warrant issued by the S.S.D. Court at the request of the Soong-Wu Military Authorities.

2.    Addressed to "Mr. Tsui You Zung, Dah Doong Printing Shop, 618 Yu Yuen Road.
      One copy each. The Kiang Hai Jih Pao and ordinary daily newspapers published at Haimen, dated Sept. 9th and 10th 1931.

3     Addressed to "Mr. Sa Faung Bah, Dah Doong Printing Shop, 618 Yu Yuen Road.
      One copy each. The Kiang Hai Jih Pao and ordinary daily newspaper published at Haimen, dated Sept. 9th and 10th 1931.
      One copy each. The Chungking Pao an ordinary daily newspaper published at Chungking dated Sep 9, 10 and 11th 1931.
      Circular letter from the Chitung Hsien Government to Sa Faung Bah, ex-magistrate of Chitung Hsien, re outstanding accounts of the Chitung Hsien Government.

3     Addressed to Mr Sa Shoa Wei, Dah Doong Printing Shop, 618 Yu Yuen Road.
      Letter from Lee Fee Yuey Kempe, asking for the repayment of a loan of $10.00 to enable him to return to Peiping.

4     Addressed to Mr Huang Han Chong, c/o Dah Doong Printing Shop, 618 Yu Yuen Road.
      Letter from his father at Chitung asking for the reason that he was not received any reply to his previous letters.

5     Addressed to Mr. D.D. Chang, 618 Yu Yuen Road.
      1 letter in German from Kate Tobias, Frankfort, Main, Germany, referring to an order from D.D. Chang for books value 1,000 Marks
      1 copy each of the International Press Correspondence dated August 25 and 27 1931.

6     Addressed to Messrs Dah Doong Printing Shop, 618 Yu Yuen Road.
      1 copy "The Chitung Pao" an ordinary daily newspaper published at Chitung, dated Sept. 8 1931.

7     Addressed to Miss Zung Ching Fung, 618 Yu Yuen Road.
      Letter of a social nature from Tseng Hui Ching, Kwong Tseong Hospital, Nanking.

Proceedings.    Mr King S Man appeared for the police.

                Mr. King:- On the 7th inst: a search warrant was executed at 618 Yu Yuen Road & 8 persons were arrested . The first two accused were handed over to the Chinese Authorities & the others found Not Guilty. Since that date a number of letters etc; have been delivered the house & the police now have them for which we ask the Court to confiscate same.

MR. 10/9

Decision. Letters & printed matter to be sent together with a letter to the Soong-Wu Military Headquarters for investigation.

Sir,

In reply to the queries by the D.C. Crime in respect of the execution of warrants No.2942-3, I beg to state that these warrants were issued at the instance of the Chinese Authorities and we had to rely on them for assistance in identifying the person mentioned on one of the warrants. I therefore applied through Mr. Loh Sih Kya, who was acting for Superintendent Tan Shao Liang, to get some one from the Soong Wu Military Headquarters to come and assist in the identification; and I was informed that Chinese Authorities were making further inquiries, and would send their man to us when inquiries were completed. I therefore locked the warrants up for safe keeping, as, so far as I could see, there was nothing on them to shew there was a fixed day for their return to Court. As I heard nothing further about this case for some days, I applied again to the Chinese Authorities, through Superintendent Tan Shao Liang, who had returned from leave, and he told me that they were sending their man over, but the person did not come till September 7, 1931, when, with the assistance of the Bubbling Well Detectives, one of the warrants was executed.

Detective Wong Ping, representative of the Chinese Authorities, gave evidence in Court which showed that they knew that the proprietor of the Dah Dong Printing Firm (大同印刷所) whom they wanted to arrest, was connected with the communists, and yet they took out a warrant to search for the Ming Sung Evening News (民聲晚報), which is deemed to be a reactionary, though not Communistic publication. Furthermore, he stated that they had to delay execution of the warrant, and keep the place under surveillance until an opportune time availed. Please

3. Raid on Printing Establishment - seizure of pro-communistic
literature - 9 arrests
1. R. 8.9.31.

At 3.30 p.m. September 7, the Municipal Police, accompanied
by representatives of the Soong Wu Military Headquarters, raided
the Dah Dong (大同) Printing Shop, F.A. 612 Yu Yuen Road, O.O.L.
on the authority of warrants issued by the Shanghai Special
District Court at the request of the above authorities in respect
of one Nyung Sien (仲先) on a charge of being in possession of
reactionary literature and to seize certain reactionary publi-
cations entitled "The Ming Sung Evening News".

The man mentioned in the warrant was absent at the time of the
visit and a search of the premises failed to produce any copies
of the newspaper in question. However, as a result of the
search, some 4,000 copies of pro-communistic books comprising
20 different kinds were seized and 9 persons found on the
premises arrested.

Among the literature seized were recent copies of the
International Press Correspondence and certain periodicals in
German addressed to "Herrn C.S. Dang" and "D.D. Chang",
F.A. 612 Yu Yuen Road. These names are believed to be
aliases used by Deng Yen-tah (邓演达), leader of the so-called
Third Party and former Commander of the 3rd Red Army Corps,
who was arrested by the Municipal Police on August 17 (Vide
I.R. 18/8/31) and subsequently extradited to the Chinese Authorities.

In view of the foregoing, it would appear that this printing
establishment was evidently the publication organ of the so-
called Third Party whose membership includes a large percentage
of communistic elements.

The arrested persons will be brought before the Second
Branch, Kiangsu High Court this morning on a charge of being
in possession of reactionary literature and a remand applied
for. Their names are as follows :-

3. 突袭印刷机构 - 查获亲共文献 - 逮捕 9 人
1. R. 1931 年 9 月 8 日。

9 月 7 日下午 3 时 30 分，公共租界警务处在淞沪卫戍司令部代表的陪同下，依据上海特区法院应上述当局要求签发的传票，对位于越界筑路区域愚园路 612 号的大东（大同）印刷所进行了突袭搜查，事由是针对一名叫仲先（Nyung Sien）的人涉嫌持有反动文献，并没收名为《明声晚报》的某些反动出版物。

传票中提到的男子在搜查时不在场，对该场所的搜查也未发现任何有关报纸的副本。然而，作为搜查的结果，查获了约 4,000 册亲共书籍，共 20 种不同种类，并逮捕了在现场发现的 9 人。

在查获的文献中，有近期的《国际新闻通讯》（International Press Correspondence）以及某些用德文写成、寄往“Herrn C.S. Dang”和“D.D. Chang”、地址为越界筑路区域愚园路 612 号的期刊。据信这些名字是邓演达使用的化名，邓演达是所谓“第三党”的领袖，曾任红军第三军团指挥官，他于 8 月 17 日被公共租界警务处逮捕（参见 1931 年 8 月 18 日情报报告），随后被引渡给中国当局。

鉴于上述情况，该印刷机构显然是所谓“第三党”的出版机关，其成员中包含大量共产主义分子。

被捕人员将于今天上午以涉嫌持有反动文献的罪名被提解至江苏高等法院第二分院，并申请还押候审。他们的姓名如下：-

My name is Lieu Ping. I am 25 years of age,
a native of Zeng Zoh(常州). I am employe as a
printer at the Dah Dong Printing Establishment, PA 612
Tu Yuen Road, and I am living there.

I have been employe with the Dah Dong Printing
Establishment for five months. I was introduced to the
shop by a friend named Sa Siao Tso ng(施小忠), whose
present whereabouts I do not know. My pay is $16. per month
Previous to this, I was employe at the Ta Ching Daung(朱锦堂)
Printing Establishment at the Great East Gate, City, for more
than a year and also at the Nanyang Printing Shop(南洋),
Small South Gate, City.

The proprietor of the Dah Dong Printing
Establishment is name Sa Paung Teh(施方德), a native of
Tsungming(崇明), about 37 years of age, and about 5' 6" in
height. He used to reside in the shop, but when the
Police came, he had left for Nantung on unknown business, about
two months ago.

I attended school at my native village and my
knowledge of Chinese is poor. I cannot thoroughly
understand the articles that I printed. I am not a member
of any political party, and I do not know if my master is
interested in politics. During the absence of my master
Wong Hui Cheng(王乃昌), Acting Accountant, takes charge of
the shop. He left the shop in the morning and has not
since returned.

I do not know for whom we print the literature seized
by the Police. The work is done quite openly.

(Signed) Lieu Ping.

else. I have been educated in Hangchow for six years.

native of Chi Tung, Haimen taken by me C.D.S. 10.
at B'Well Stn. on the 7-9-31 and translated by Y.B. Pu.

states;

I have been educated in my native country for seven
years. I am now living at 612 Yu Yuen Road, the Dah Dong Printing
Establishment owned by Sz Faung Pah, where I am employed as a
typesetter apprentice through the introduction of my fellow-country
men named Sung Yui Sung in March this year. As I have only
remained in the shop for about 10 days, I went to homeland owing
only/
to me being sick, and I arrived back to Shanghai two weeks ago.
I haven't started to work yet. I don't know what were the books
printed in the shop. I had never seen my master since my return
from sick leave.
